newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says sugar export tender result on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says sugar export tender result on Friday.

text.p: Turkey's state sugar refiner Turkseker said on Thursday it would announce the result of a 50,000-tonne white sugar export tender on Friday after the approval of the company board.
"The sub-commissions have completed their assessment and we will present the result to the board tomorrow which will meet at 3 p.m. (1300 GMT)," said Selahattin Hun, general manager of Turkseker.
"But I can tell we have satisfactory bids to sell the entire 50,000 tonnes," he told Reuters.
A Turkseker official earlier said they might consider to split the 50,000-tonne offer into two or three parts.
Traders said the tender, which closed on Monday, had attracted more local company interest than international companies because of the tender terms.

Turkseker required that the sugar be delivered on a free-on-truck basis to the buyer from several refineries at various locations in Turkey. The buyers should also give a letter of guarantee equal to the value of their purchase.
Traders said they expected the sugar to be delivered from the refineries at Elbistan, Agri, Kars, Bor and Carsamba.

They said the bidders included local food and commodities traders of Lebsan, Baykur, Naptat, Yilmazlar, Rotel, Ram and Fissan, and named E D & F Man and Andre among the few international companies which participated.
They said the prices at the tender by some competing local companies ran as high as "Paris plus $20".
They said several companies withdrew their bids after some aggressive local food traders with trade connections with Iran and Georgia bid higher prices.
Traders said Lebsan bid for 46,000 tonnes, Baykur for 10,000 tonnes and other local companies for smaller amounts. Turkseker does not accept bids lower than 2,0000 tonnes.
